 Qatari emir, Trump discuss mediation efforts to end regional crisis
 06-Nov-2026, 16:25 06 Nov 2026, 16:25 AFP Share The high-profile exchange was part of intensified diplomacy as Gulf nations feared a possible resumption of US strikes on Iran.
 Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and Donald Trump discussed ‘diplomatic efforts aimed at de-escalating tensions in the region’ during a phone call on Friday. (EPA Images pic) 
 DOHA : US President Donald Trump on Friday called Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani to discuss efforts to end the US-Iran war, amid a diplomatic push to avoid a new round of conflict. 
 The high-profile exchange was the latest in a flurry of diplomatic phone calls that saw Iran’s top diplomat speaking to his counterparts in the Gulf amid fears that Trump could resume strikes despite major losses in midterms elections.
 Sheikh Tamim received a call from Trump, according to his office, the Amiri Diwan, during which the pair discussed “diplomatic efforts aimed at de-escalating tensions in the region” undertaken by mediator Qatar.
 The Emir “emphasised the importance of continuing dialogue and relying on diplomatic means to settle disputes and prevent further escalation,” the statement read.
